register.name: Resilience and Sustainability Facility
register.detail: IMF · Approved 27 April 2026 · 21 months · first review completed 28 September 2026
register.note: About US$266 million at approval; SDR 17.62 million released on the first review
register.text: The IMF’s climate resilience arrangement for Liberia, alongside the Extended Credit Facility. The Ministry of Finance says it supports climate adaptation, resilient infrastructure and pandemic preparedness. The first review, completed on 28 September 2026, released SDR 17.62 million.

register.name: Extended Credit Facility
register.detail: IMF · Approved 25 September 2024 · 40 months · 60% of quota · fourth review completed 28 September 2026
register.note: SDR 96.5 million (about US$131.67 million) disbursed after the fourth review, which released SDR 19.3 million
register.text: The IMF’s main lending programme with Liberia, supporting macroeconomic stability, debt sustainability, a more resilient financial sector and governance reforms. Its priorities include domestic revenue, with the Value Added Tax to be implemented in 2027, and the completion of bank restructuring.

register.name: Regional Distributed Access through Renewable Energy Solutions (Regional DARES), first phase
register.detail: World Bank · Approved 22 June 2026 · with Benin, the Central African Republic and Sierra Leone · first phase of an $853 million programme
register.note: $200 million for the four nations together; the share of Liberia is not stated
register.text: Finances solar home systems, mini-grids and other off-grid technologies for rural, isolated and underserved communities in four nations. It serves energy, the standard furthest from reach: 34.9% of Liberians have electricity and 1% cook with clean fuels.

register.name: Western Africa Regional Digital Integration Program, second operation (WARDIP2)
register.detail: World Bank · Approved 10 March 2026 for Benin, Liberia and Sierra Leone · Liberia’s agreement signed June 2026
register.note: Liberia’s share of the $137 million approved for the three nations
register.text: Expands broadband access and digital connectivity, strengthens cybersecurity and digital governance, and supports digital entrepreneurship, e-commerce and digital payments towards a single digital market in West Africa. It serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Regional Emergency Solar Power Intervention Project (RESPITE), additional financing
register.detail: World Bank · Signed in Harrisburg, Montserrado County, June 2026 · Mount Coffee Solar Park from 20 MWp to 30 MWp
register.note: With battery energy storage and improvements to the national energy network
register.text: Enlarges the Mount Coffee Solar Park from 20 MWp to 30 MWp, deploys battery energy storage systems and improves the national energy network. It serves energy, the standard furthest from reach.

register.name: Southeastern Corridor Road Asset Management Project (SECRAMP), second additional financing
register.detail: World Bank · Signed June 2026 · 100 km Ganta–Tappita corridor
register.note: To complete the works under way on the corridor
register.text: Finances the completion of ongoing works along the 100-kilometre Ganta–Tappita corridor. It serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Second Resilient and Inclusive Growth Development Policy Financing
register.detail: World Bank (IDA) · Approved 2 June 2026 · budget support tied to reforms
register.note: Includes support for the financial viability of the Liberia Electricity Corporation
register.text: Budget support for reforms in resource mobilisation, public financial management, transparency and accountability, and the foundations for private sector development. It also supports the financial viability of the Liberia Electricity Corporation and disaster risk financing, which reach the energy and livelihood standards.

register.name: Upgrading of the Salayea to Konia Road Project
register.detail: OPEC Fund · Approved 25 March 2026 (release of 24 March 2026) · tranche loan · 50 km
register.note: Up to 300,000 people to benefit; travel time from 160 to 45 minutes
register.text: A tranche loan to rehabilitate 50 km of a key corridor linking Bong County to the Sierra Leone border, to all-weather asphalt standard. It serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Excellence in Learning in Liberia (EXCEL) Project
register.detail: World Bank (IDA) · Approved by the Board, release of 10 June 2025 · 2,337 public primary schools
register.note: IDA credit, with a $28.7 million grant from the Global Partnership for Education
register.text: Improves foundational learning and access in public primary schools, reaching 350,000 students in the last grade of early childhood education and all six grades of primary, with training for about 12,000 teachers. It serves education, where 44.5% of young people complete lower secondary school.

register.name: Salayea–Konia Road
register.detail: BADEA · Loan agreement signed in Vienna, 23 June 2026 · 50 km in Lofa County
register.note: A BADEA grant of US$700,000 supports health services along the Gbarnga–Voinjama corridor
register.text: Finances the upgrading of the Salayea–Konia Road in Lofa County, within a package with the Kuwait Fund for Arab Economic Development, the Saudi Fund for Development and the OPEC Fund. It serves the livelihood standard, and the health standard through the clinics along the corridor.

register.name: Renewable Energy for Electrification in Liberia (REEL), additional loan
register.detail: African Development Fund · Approved by the Board 25 November 2025 · Gbedin Falls, Nimba County · 9.34 MW
register.note: Covers a cost overrun on the hydropower plant and related infrastructure
register.text: An additional concessional loan to complete the 9.34 megawatt run-of-river hydropower plant at Gbedin Falls in Nimba County and its related infrastructure. It serves energy, the standard furthest from reach.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of the land under forest, 2024
items.text: Two thirds of the land under forest: carbon that can earn as it stands.

items.name: The Fresh Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water a person, 2022
items.text: Among the most fresh water per person in Africa.

items.name: The Clean Grid
items.label: Of electricity from renewable sources, 2021
items.text: Power from water and sun already flows; every new connection can be clean.

items.name: The Ground
items.label: Of GDP from natural resource rents, 2021
items.text: What lies under the land already earns; the task is to turn the rent into lasting assets.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 39.1% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.

items.name: Liberia-American Poultry Farm
items.text: An egg farm in Bomi County, established in 2021, which its managing director says has capacity for over 550,000 birds and daily egg production of roughly 350,000 for the domestic market. More than 450 Liberians are employed.

items.name: Easy Solar
items.text: Sells solar power on pay-as-you-go terms through a network of agents that reaches remote communities across Sierra Leone and Liberia. Since 2016 it has delivered solar access to over one million people across West Africa.

items.name: Green Gold Liberia
items.text: A social enterprise that produces and distributes bio-briquettes, biogas and biofuels. In April 2026 it led a local initiative that trained people to turn organic waste into solid fuel and to build clean cooking stoves, which are being prepared for community use.

items.name: Rising Academies
items.text: Operates public schools under the Liberia Education Advancement Program, in which the Ministry of Education contracts private organisations to run selected public schools. It serves more than 50,000 students in Ghana, Liberia and Sierra Leone.

items.name: Last Mile Health
items.text: A non-profit and the longest-serving community health partner to Liberia’s Ministry of Health. The national community health programme reached full scale in June 2024, with paid community health workers in every district providing primary care to more than one million Liberians.

items.name: J-Palm Liberia
items.text: Buys palm kernels from smallholder farmers in rural Liberia that were once wasted and cold presses them into oil for soaps, moisturisers and hair conditioners. Its traceability app, which pays harvesters through mobile money, has been rolled out to 20 communities.
